references.text: Joseph was made master over Pharaoh's house and over all he owned, a direct description of the exaltation depicted in Gen 41:42.

Daniel was clothed in purple and given a gold chain around his neck by King Belshazzar as recognition of his wisdom, a clear parallel to Joseph who was clothed in linen and given a gold chain by Pharaoh.
The king took off the signet ring he had taken from Haman and gave it to Mordecai – a direct parallel to how Pharaoh removed his ring and gave it to Joseph as a sign of transferred authority.
The king took the ring from his hand and gave it to Haman, showing that handing over the king's signet ring was a sign of delegated power, just as Pharaoh did with Joseph.
The prodigal son was clothed in the best robe and given a ring on his finger as a sign of restoration and honor, a parallel to Joseph who was honored with a ring and fine clothes by Pharaoh.
Both verses document Joseph's transition from prisoner to prince, where verse 14 shows the preparation and verse 42 the actual installation with symbols of authority.
Both verses illustrate Joseph's rising authority: v. 39:4 shows trust in a private household, while v. 41:42 shows full power over the nation through royal symbols.
Both verses describe ceremonial clothing that marks appointment to a high office (high priest vs. vizier) with symbolism for authority and service.
